Install with `composer require thesis/http` on 64-bit PHP 8.6+ with ext-zlib.

The [client](#client) and [server](#server) share [messages](#messages) and the same HTTP/1 implementation.

## Messages

Clients and servers use the same `Request` and `Response`. Use `with…` methods to derive a message
with different metadata. The original and its copies share one right to take the body.

```php
use Thesis\Http\Request;
use Thesis\Http\Response;

$request = Request::get('https://example.org/search')
    ->withQueryParameter('tag', ['php', 'http'])
    ->withHeader('Accept', 'application/json');

$response = (new Response(body: 'ok'))->withAddedHeader('Set-Cookie', 'theme=dark');
$body = $response->takeBody();
$bytes = $body->readAll();
$trailers = $body->trailers();
```

Requests and responses default to `Thesis\Http\EMPTY_BODY`, a reusable empty body with empty trailers.
Pass a string or an unread body to supply a payload. Give the message exclusive access until
`takeBody()` transfers the reader to its caller. Dropping the last message copy closes an unclaimed body. A second call through any metadata copy raises
`LogicException`. A proxy can pass `$request->withUri($upstream)` to the client and return its response
directly. Taking either body also transfers its trailers. Use `withBody()` to supply a replacement.

Read incrementally or call `readAll()` for the whole payload (8 MiB by default). Pass `limit:` to choose a byte limit.
Overflow and read failures close the body. After any bytes have been consumed,
collecting the whole body raises `LogicException`. Close the reader to release its resources.
Supply ready trailer fields with `new StringBody($bytes, $trailers)`. A streaming body can determine
its fields while reading. Calling `trailers()` while fields are still pending raises `LogicException`.

A client middleware that may resend an upload takes the body before calling the next handler.
It passes `$request->withBody($body)` on the first attempt. When policy permits another attempt
and the body implements `ReplayableBody`, it passes `$request->withBody($body->fresh())`.
This creates a new handoff with its own reader and trailers.
`StringBody` supports replay. Headers, methods, status codes and ordered query parameters
are shared by requests and responses.

## `Headers`

`Headers` is immutable. It treats names as case-insensitive and can store several lines under the same name.

```php
$headers = new Headers([
    'Accept' => ['text/html', 'application/json;q=0.9'],
    'User-Agent' => 'thesis',
]);

$headers->has('accept');          // true
$headers->get('ACCEPT');          // 'text/html, application/json;q=0.9'
$headers->all('accept');          // ['text/html', 'application/json;q=0.9']
$headers->get('cookie');          // null

$headers = $headers
    ->with('accept', 'text/plain')           // replaces the lines of the field
    ->withAdded('set-cookie', 'a=1')         // adds a line
    ->withAdded('set-cookie', 'b=2')
    ->without('user-agent');

foreach ($headers as $name => $lines) {
    // 'accept' => ['text/plain'], 'set-cookie' => ['a=1', 'b=2']
}
```

- Names are stored in lowercase, as HTTP/2 requires.
- `get()` joins the lines of a field with a comma, as RFC 9110 defines. `set-cookie` is the exception:
  its lines cannot be joined, use `all()`.
- `Headers` throws `\ValueError` if a name is invalid or a value contains a forbidden control character.
  So user input with `\r\n` in it cannot add a line to a message (response splitting). Spaces and tabs
  around a value are trimmed.

## Client

A URL string sends a GET. Reuse the client across calls. Wrap both the request and the read in an async
timeout to apply one deadline to connection acquisition, redirects and downloading the body.

```php
use Thesis\Http\Client;
use function Thesis\Async\timeout;
use function Thesis\Time\sec;

$client = new Client();
$bytes = timeout(sec(10), static fn() => $client->send('https://example.com/')->takeBody()->readAll());
```

Send an HTTP/1.1 request inside a Thesis async scope. The final response head is available as soon as
`send()` returns. Read the body under the deadline you want for the download. The client supplies a body that implements
`Closer`. Close an unfinished body to close its connection immediately. A permanent read failure or dropping the last
reference to an unfinished body also closes the connection. A malformed response head or body raises
`Thesis\Io\IoException` during `send()` or while reading the body.

```php
use Thesis\Http\Request;
use Thesis\Http\Client;
use Thesis\Http\Response;
use Uri\Rfc3986\Uri;
use function Thesis\Async\timeout;
use function Thesis\Time\sec;

$request = new Request('GET', new Uri('https://example.com/'));
$client = new Client();
$response = timeout(sec(5), static fn() => $client->send($request));
$status = $response->status;
$response->takeBody()->close();
```

Use `withResponse()` to close the body when a callback returns or throws:

```php
$status = $client->withResponse('https://example.com/', static fn(Response $response) => $response->status);
```

Reuse the same client across requests to share connections for the same scheme, host and port.
A fixed-length body releases its socket on the last byte. A chunked body releases it after the trailers.
Take the body once, read until EOF to reuse the connection, then call `$body->trailers()` for the final fields. A bodyless response releases it immediately.
The byte limit `maxResponseHeadBytes` covers informational and final response headers together (default 64 KiB).
An outstanding body keeps its own socket and counts toward `maxConnectionsPerOrigin` (default 10).
Further callers for that origin wait for a slot. The client retains up to `maxIdleConnections` sockets across
all origins (default 32). Set it to zero to close each socket after its exchange.
If a peer closes an idle connection, the next request opens a new one. A disconnect during a request
propagates to the caller. Automatic retries are opt-in.

HTTPS verifies the peer through thesis/net.
Pass a Net ClientTls configuration to the constructor to use a private CA.
The transport takes and closes the request body before it reads the response.
For another send, supply a new body with `withBody()` or build a new request.

### Middleware

Pass `middleware: []` for a single exchange with the original content encoding. By default the client runs
`FollowRedirects` then `DecodeContent`. Supplying a list replaces the defaults. A middleware implements
`Thesis\Http\Client\Middleware` with `handle(Request $request, callable $next): Response`. It can return a cached response, change the request
using `withHeader()` or `withBody()`, call `$next($request)`, or wrap the response body. Close intermediate responses before
sending another request. Middleware before `FollowRedirects` sees the application request once.
Middleware after it sees each destination. Scope credential injection to the intended origin.

`FollowRedirects` follows up to ten redirects. It resolves relative locations, turns a POST into a GET on
301/302, and drops the body on 303. For 307/308 it can resend a `ReplayableBody` with its original method.
It returns the intermediate response when the body cannot be replayed, the limit is reached, the location
is unusable, or HTTPS would downgrade to HTTP. Across origins only allowlisted negotiation and content
headers carry over.

`DecodeContent` negotiates gzip and deflate, decompresses the stream as it is read, and preserves trailers.
Set `Accept-Encoding` yourself or send a range request to keep control of the encoded bytes.

Place `new RetryRequests(maxRetries: 1)` last in the middleware list to retry an idempotent method with
a `ReplayableBody` on a connection, read or write failure before the response arrives. It opens an independent
reader on each retry. After `send()` returns, download errors propagate to the consumer.

A custom `connector` receives the origin host, port and optional `ClientTls` and returns a connected
`Thesis\Net\Socket`. It runs only when the pool needs a new socket. Each client owns its pool.

### Form uploads

`Form::urlEncoded()` builds a POST request. Use a list of values to repeat a name.
`Form::multipart()` accepts ordered fields and files. Pass an unread `Thesis\Io\Reader` to upload a file or
forward a stream. Construction only prepares the part headers. Sending the request reads the payload in chunks.

```php
use Thesis\Http\Client\Form;
use Thesis\Http\Client\FormPart;

$request = Form::urlEncoded('https://example.com/search', ['tag' => ['news', 'science']]);
$upload = Form::multipart('https://example.com/files', [
    new FormPart('description', 'Monthly report'),
    new FormPart('file', $reader, filename: 'report.pdf', contentType: 'application/pdf'),
]);
$status = $client->withResponse($upload, static fn($response) => $response->status);
```

A string, an unread `StringReader`, or a `Body` of known size contributes its length automatically.
For another reader, pass `size:` to send exactly that many bytes. An unknown length selects chunked transfer.
Closing the multipart request body closes every part reader that implements `Closer`.

### HTTP proxy

```php
use Thesis\Http\Headers;
use Thesis\Http\Client;
use Thesis\Http\Client\HttpProxy;

$proxy = new HttpProxy('proxy.internal', 3128, new Headers(['Proxy-Authorization' => $proxyCredential]));
$response = (new Client(connector: $proxy))->send('https://example.com/');
```

The client connects to the proxy over plaintext HTTP and requests a CONNECT tunnel for the origin.
If the proxy refuses CONNECT or returns a malformed response, opening the tunnel throws `Thesis\Net\ConnectFailed`.
For HTTPS the client negotiates TLS inside the tunnel and verifies the origin's certificate.

## Server

Serve HTTP/1 requests on a TCP or Unix listener. Each connection runs in its own task.
Requests on the same connection run in order. The handler receives the shared `Thesis\Http\Request`
and a `Thesis\Http\Server\Context` with connection information. It returns a `Thesis\Http\Response`.
`Thesis\Http\Server` defines two PHPStan types for this signature. The server constructor accepts
`Handler` and stores the resulting closure as `HandlerClosure`. Import the latter with
`@phpstan-import-type HandlerClosure from \Thesis\Http\Server`.

### Routing

Build a `Router` once and pass it directly to `Server`. The constructor accepts an iterable of routes. Pass one method or a non-empty list of methods to each `Route`. Each route handler receives the request
and the connection context. Inside the route handler and its middleware, `Thesis\Http\Server\routeMatch($request)` returns the active match.
Use `Thesis\Http\Server\routeParam($request, $name)` to read one decoded parameter. It returns null when the parameter is absent or the request has no active match.
Outside dispatch `routeMatch()` returns null. The match’s `method` and `pattern` identify the selected route.
`param($name)` returns a decoded parameter or null, and `$match->params` contains all parameters.

```php
use Thesis\Http\Method;
use Thesis\Http\Response;
use Thesis\Http\Server\Config;
use Thesis\Http\Server\Route;
use Thesis\Http\Server\Router;
use Thesis\Http\Server;
use function Thesis\Http\Server\routeParam;

$router = new Router([
    new Route(Method::GET, '/users/me', static fn() => new Response(body: 'Current user')),
    new Route(Method::GET, '/users/{id}', static fn($request) => new Response(body: routeParam($request, 'id') ?? '')),
]);

$server = new Server(new Config(8080), $router);
```

Patterns start with a slash. A placeholder such as `{user_id}` consumes a nonempty segment.
Names start with an ASCII letter or underscore and may also contain digits. Each name occurs once.
Use trailing optional segments (`/archive/{year?}/{month?}`) or capture the remaining path
with a final `{path+}` (nonempty) or `{path*}` (possibly empty). The remainder keeps its slashes.
Omitted optional parameters are absent unless supplied in the route's `defaults` string map.

A segment can combine literals and parameters, for example `/reports/{year}-{month}.csv`.
Pass PCRE fragments by parameter name in `requirements`, for example `['year' => '[0-9]{4}']`.
A requirement matches its parameter, including slashes for a remainder. The router tries literal, constrained or compound,
ordinary parameter, then remainder at each position. Overlapping expressions at the same
position are tried in registration order. An explicit endpoint precedes an omitted suffix.
Duplicate method and path shapes fail during construction.

`$router->lookup($request)` returns the selected RouteMatch or null without calling a handler
or emitting an event. Dispatch checks the method after selecting the complete path.
An explicit HEAD wins over the GET fallback. A mismatch yields 405 with Allow, an unknown path 404.

Matching uses the raw URI path. Dot segments, plus signs and trailing slashes keep their meaning.
End a pattern with `[/]` to accept one optional slash. For example, `/docs[/]` matches both `/docs` and `/docs/`.
A remainder must end its pattern and captures trailing slashes itself.
An absolute URI with an empty path matches `/`. The special targets `OPTIONS *` and authority-form `CONNECT` have no route path.
Percent escapes are decoded once. An invalid escape, an encoded slash or a NUL yields 400.
For example, `/users/a%252Fb` passes `a%2Fb` to the handler.

By default, routing errors and server-generated 500 responses carry a small HTML page with the status code
and its standard reason phrase when known. Pass an optional `Server\ErrorHandler` to the server to customize routing errors and 500 responses:

```php
$errorHandler = new class implements \Thesis\Http\Server\ErrorHandler {
    public function handleError(int $status, \Thesis\Http\Request $request): \Thesis\Http\Response
    {
        return new \Thesis\Http\Response($status, body: "Request failed ($status)");
    }
};

$server = new Server(new Config(8080), new Router($routes), errorHandler: $errorHandler);
```

Return the supplied status. The router sets `Allow` on a 405. Protocol rejections still have an empty body.
An explicit error response from an application handler passes through as returned.

### Streaming echo

```php
use Thesis\Async\Group;
use Thesis\Http\Request;
use Thesis\Http\Response;
use Thesis\Http\Server\Config;
use Thesis\Http\Server;
use function Thesis\Async\awaitShutdownSignal;
use function Thesis\Async\group;

$server = new Server(
    config: new Config(8080),
    handler: static fn(Request $request) => new Response(
        body: $request->takeBody(),
    ),
);

group(static function (Group $group) use ($server) {
    $server->start($group);
    awaitShutdownSignal();
    $server->stop();
});
```

The response reads from the incoming body as it is written. A chunked request's trailers become available
after its terminating chunk. The server reads them from the body and writes them in the last chunk of the response.

From the Thesis monorepo, run the example in Docker.

```sh
docker compose run --rm -p 127.0.0.1:8080:8080 php php packages/http/examples/echo.php
```

In another terminal, send two requests with one curl process. The first uses chunked transfer encoding.
Curl prints the number of new connections it opened for the second request; expect zero.

```sh
curl --http1.1 -sS -H 'Transfer-Encoding: chunked' --data-binary 'one' http://127.0.0.1:8080/first \
  --next -sS --data-binary 'two' -w '\nnew connections: %{num_connects}\n' http://127.0.0.1:8080/second
```

### Server middleware

Use `Pipeline::wrap()` to wrap a handler and pass it to the server. It collects the middleware from an iterable
in iteration order, ignoring keys. An empty iterable returns the original handler. The same handler can serve
concurrent requests.

```php
use Thesis\Http\Server;
use Thesis\Http\Server\Pipeline;

$pipeline = Pipeline::wrap($handler, [$accessLog, $authorization]);
$server = new Server($config, $pipeline);
```

The first middleware receives the request first and the response last.
Each layer receives `handle(Request $request, Context $context, callable $next)`. It can use
`$context->errorHandler->handleError(403, $request)` to format an error with the server’s configured error handler.
Server middleware can return a response directly or call `$next()`. After that call returns or throws,
the middleware can call `$next()` again while its own `handle()` is running. Overlapping calls to the
same `$next` and calls after its `handle()` has returned or thrown raise a `LogicException`.

Each call starts at the same next layer with the same request and connection context.
The server streams incoming bodies and the pipeline does not buffer them for replay. Once a layer calls
`takeBody()`, another call on the same request throws a `LogicException`, even if the reader consumed
no bytes. A `ReplayableBody` lets its owner open another reader, but the request still hands off its body only once.

When a handler deserializes the body into a DTO, retry the operation that uses the DTO after deserialization.
A retry runs downstream code again, so any side effects from an earlier attempt must be safe to repeat.

### Connection lifetime

The server constructor takes a `Config` and the request handler and does no I/O.
Pass an integer port to listen on `127.0.0.1`. With `new Config(0)`, the OS chooses the port.
To specify the address, pass a string such as `'0.0.0.0:8080'` or `'[::1]:8080'`, or pass an `InetAddress`.
For Unix, pass an absolute socket path such as `'/run/app.sock'`. Use `UnixEndpoint` for a relative path.
Both endpoint types let you set `backlog`, which defaults to 511. `TcpEndpoint` also takes `reusePort` and `noDelay`.

`$server->start($group)` binds the endpoint and returns once the server is ready. A bind failure throws
`Thesis\Net\ListenFailed` from `start()`. With TCP port zero, `$server->address` gives the assigned port.
Call `$server->stop()` outside request handlers to stop accepting clients and wait for shutdown.
The server closes idle sockets and lets active handlers
and response writers finish until the shutdown deadline. Cancelling the serving scope also stops the server.
The example uses ext-pcntl and handles SIGINT and SIGTERM by closing the listener.

If the handler throws
before the final response starts, the client receives a 500. Once a final response has started,
a failure closes the connection. Each connection runs independently of the others.

When the handler leaves the request body unread, the server finishes writing its response and closes the
connection. An echo or another streaming response may still read the request body after the handler returns.
A fixed-length request is complete when its final payload byte is read. A chunked request is complete when
the decoder has consumed the terminating chunk and all its trailers.

### Server events

The server uses an empty dispatcher by default. Pass a `Thesis\Dispatcher` as the named `dispatcher` argument to observe events.
Subscribe by the event class in `Thesis\Http\Server\Event`. Listeners run synchronously in the emitting task. Handlers and middleware can publish their own events to the same dispatcher with `$context->dispatcher->dispatch($event)`.

| Event | When the server dispatches it |
| --- | --- |
| `ServerStarted` | The listener is ready, with its bound address and whether TLS is enabled. |
| `ServerStopping` | The listener has closed and graceful shutdown starts, with the number of open connections and the shutdown timeout. |
| `ServerStopped` | The serving group and its connection tasks have finished. Includes the number of open connections forced closed at the shutdown deadline. |
| `ConnectionAccepted`, `ConnectionClosed` | A connection task starts or releases its socket. Both carry the local and remote addresses. |
| `RequestHeadRejected` | The parser rejected the head, before the server attempts the error response. Carries the status and parser diagnostic. |
| `RequestStarted` | The server accepted a parsed request head. Carries the request, including when the server will reject its size or expectation. |
| `RouteMatched` | The router is about to invoke a matched handler. Carries the request and the match, including the selected route method. |
| `RequestEnded` | Processing of a parsed request ended, including cancellation and failed writes. Carries the intended final status if available, whether the whole response was written, and elapsed time since the parsed head. |
| `TlsHandshakeFailed`, `ConnectionHandlingFailed` | An exception escaped TLS negotiation or HTTP processing. A listener can accept both with the union type `TlsHandshakeFailed\|ConnectionHandlingFailed`. Each carries the original exception and the connection addresses. |

A malformed request head never starts an exchange. A handler exception followed by a successful 500 write produces
both a finished request and a server error. A handler that returns a 500 produces only the normal request events.
The server dispatches `RequestEnded` directly when processing leaves the exchange, including on cancellation.
The three request events expose the request as `$event->request`. Use its object identity to correlate events,
including concurrent requests to the same URI. The handler receives this same object. Calling `takeBody()` in a listener
claims the body for that listener. For an early 413 or 417 the server exposes the parsed headers and an empty body.

### Server logging

Pass a PSR-3 logger to `ServerLogger`. It logs startup and shutdown at info, HTTP failures at error,
and TLS failures and rejected request heads at debug. The TCP startup message includes a URL with the bound port.
Wildcard listeners use a loopback URL and keep the bound address in the log context. Enable the optional access log to record each
finished request at info, including its method, path, status, write outcome and duration
in milliseconds. The path excludes the query string.

```php
use Thesis\Dispatcher;
use Thesis\Http\Server;
use Thesis\Http\Server\ServerLogger;

$server = new Server($config, $handler, dispatcher: new Dispatcher([new ServerLogger($logger, accessLog: true)]));
```

### Limits

Pass limits and timeouts as named arguments of `Config`, for example `new Config($endpoint, maxConnections: 256)`.
Sizes count bytes. Durations use `Time\Duration`, for example `Thesis\Time\sec(5)`.

| Option | Default | Applies to |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `maxConnections` | 1024 | Accepted connections, including idle ones |
| `maxRequestsPerConnection` | `null` (unlimited) | Set a positive integer to limit requests per connection |
| `maxHeadBytes` | 64 KiB | The request line and fields, including the terminating empty line |
| `maxBodyBytes` | 16 MiB | Payload after decoding HTTP/1 framing |
| `headTimeout` | 10 s | Receipt of the complete head |
| `idleTimeout` | 30 s | Waiting for the next request on a persistent connection |
| `bodyIdleTimeout` | 30 s | A transport read while receiving the request body |
| `writeTimeout` | 30 s | A transport write |
| `tlsHandshakeTimeout` | 10 s | Negotiation when a TLS configuration is supplied |
| `shutdownTimeout` | 5 s | Finishing active exchanges after shutdown starts |

### TLS and request expectations

Pass a `Thesis\Net\ServerTls` configuration through the `tls` argument of `Config` to enable HTTPS.
The TLS handshake runs in the task for the accepted socket. The handler can inspect the negotiated details
through `$context->tls`. Use `http/1.1` when configuring ALPN for this server.

For HTTP/1.1 uploads with `Expect: 100-continue`, a handler can reject a request from its headers or read
its body. A body read sends the interim response if the client is waiting. A successful streaming response
can also consume the request body later. The server sends Continue before that response starts. A known length above the
configured limit gets 413 before the server accepts the upload. An unsupported expectation gets 417.

The server implements HTTP message exchanges. Protocol switching, CONNECT tunnels and HTTP/2 are outside
this proof of concept.

## HTTP/1 parsing

The client derives `Host` from the URI. Both client and server choose the framing from the body and trailers.
Eligible `HEAD` and `304` responses preserve an explicit `Content-Length` as representation metadata.

The server rejects malformed request heads and closes the connection. Examples include:

- a line that ends with a bare `\n` or contains a bare `\r`, a folded line, a space before the colon of a field;
- a name that is not a token, a control character in a value;
- `Content-Length` together with `Transfer-Encoding`; a `Content-Length` that is repeated, is a list (`5, 5`),
  has a sign or an embedded space, or has more than 18 digits;
- a transfer coding other than exactly `chunked` (`gzip, chunked` is rejected too), and any transfer coding
  in HTTP/1.0;
- an HTTP/1.1 request without `Host` or with two, a `Host` that is not a host with an optional port;
- a target that is none of these: an RFC 3986 path, an `http` or `https` URI, `*` for `OPTIONS`, a host
  and a port for `CONNECT`; a target with a fragment or user info;
- more than 100 fields.

For a request-target starting with a slash, the parser percent-encodes `[ ] \ ^ `` ` `` { | }` in the path or query.
Browsers send these bytes unescaped (`?filter[name]=x`), and an RFC 3986 URI cannot hold them.

The fields that belong to the connection, and the fields that `Connection` names, are removed from the headers:
they are meant for this hop only, and a proxy must not forward them.
